name: The Persian Ironwood of Artis

location.address: Artis Park, Plantage Kerklaan 38-40, 1018 CZ Amsterdam

verified_sources: https://maps.amsterdam.nl/bomen_bijzonder/ (Gemeente Amsterdam Bijzondere Bomen register, dataset 561, register_id N1763, plant year 1910, trunk girth 205 cm, status Beschermwaardige houtopstand)
access: Paid entry, part of Artis zoo and botanical garden
verify_notes: About 30m from the already-published Heimanseik (ams_001), near the Aldabra giant tortoise enclosure. Officially designated by the city as a Beschermwaardige houtopstand (protection-worthy stand) under register id N1763, planted 1910, trunk girth 205 cm. Independently named in a 2020s oost-online.nl profile of Artis's tree collection by Jan de Jong (an Artis groundskeeper/tree specialist), who calls this ijzerhout (ironwood) his personal favourite in the whole park, describing it as 'warrig en grillig' (tangled and irregular) with branches that fuse into each other as they grow, a genuine growth habit of the species. Persian Ironwood is famous for exceptional autumn colour (reds, oranges, purples on the same tree) and for peeling, mottled bark similar to a plane tree's. Good story hook: a park specialist singling this specific, unglamorous-looking tree out as his favourite over 800+ other trees and 200+ species in the park is a strong human angle. No photo hunted this pass, per brief.

name: The Coast Redwood of Artis

location.address: Artis Park, Plantage Kerklaan 38-40, 1018 CZ Amsterdam

verified_sources: https://maps.amsterdam.nl/bomen_bijzonder/ (Gemeente Amsterdam Bijzondere Bomen register, dataset 561, register_id N5627, plant year circa 1920, trunk girth 271 cm, status Beschermwaardige houtopstand)
access: Paid entry, part of Artis zoo and botanical garden
verify_notes: Register plant year is 'circa 1920' (approximate in the source itself, not our rounding). Located near the Artis planetarium per the independent oost-online.nl article, which describes it as the world's tallest tree species (up to 115m in its native California range) and singles it out among Artis's collection. A coast redwood of this age and 271cm girth reaching real size this far from its native range and this far north is itself the visual hook: an unmistakably conifer, unmistakably enormous tree in the middle of a 19th-century Dutch zoo. Pairs naturally with the Persian Ironwood (ams_012) and Heimanseik (ams_001) on the same short walk through Artis. No photo hunted this pass, per brief.

name: The Twisted Catalpa of the Hortus

location.address: Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam, Plantage Middenlaan 2A, 1018 DD Amsterdam

verified_sources: https://maps.amsterdam.nl/bomen_bijzonder/ (Gemeente Amsterdam Bijzondere Bomen register, dataset 561, register_id N1776, plant year 1910, trunk girth 318 cm, status Beschermwaardige houtopstand)

https://www.bomenstichting.nl/images/Mon_bomen_Amsterdam_2021_WEB.pdf (Bomenstichting, 'Langs monumentale bomen in het centrum van Amsterdam', 5th ed. 2021, entry 'Trompetboom, Catalpa bignonioides, NR 1690871 op monumentalebomen.nl, PLANTJAAR 1910-1920, HORTUS BOTANICUS AMSTERDAM')
access: Paid entry, Hortus Botanicus ticket required
verify_notes: Two independent sources agree closely: municipal register plant year 1910, national Bomenstichting guide gives 1910-1920, both citing a trunk girth of roughly 3 metres (register: 318cm exactly). The Bomenstichting guide, an official printed Amsterdam walking-tour booklet (partly funded by the Gemeente, author Hans Kaljee), describes this specific specimen as having 'a beautiful twisted trunk' (prachtig gedraaide stam) and large cream-and-yellow trumpet-shaped flowers with 20cm leaves; the species is native to the southeastern US and known in Dutch as trompetboom (trumpet tree) or bonenboom (bean tree) for its long pod-like seed cases. Repels mosquitoes and flies per the same source, a nice visitor-facing detail. Genuinely visually distinctive (twisted trunk) rather than just old.
best_time_hint: Flowers in summer (roughly July), per general Catalpa bignonioides phenology; not independently confirmed for this specimen this pass, leave for a phenology-focused pass to set best_time formally.

name: The Shellbark Hickory of the Hortus
age_estimate: roughly 76 to 114 years (sources disagree on planting year)

location.address: Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam, Plantage Middenlaan 2A, 1018 DD Amsterdam

verified_sources: https://maps.amsterdam.nl/bomen_bijzonder/ (Gemeente Amsterdam Bijzondere Bomen register, dataset 561, register_id N1768, plant year 1950, trunk girth 251 cm, status Beschermwaardige houtopstand)

https://www.bomenstichting.nl/images/Mon_bomen_Amsterdam_2021_WEB.pdf (Bomenstichting guide, entry 'Koningsnoot, Carya laciniosa, NR 1686144 op monumentalebomen.nl, PLANTJAAR 1912, HORTUS BOTANICUS AMSTERDAM', described as 'de oudste koningsnoot van Nederland' / the oldest shellbark hickory in the Netherlands)
access: Paid entry, Hortus Botanicus ticket required
verify_notes: SOURCE CONFLICT, flagged rather than resolved: the municipal register gives plant year 1950 (girth 251cm); the Bomenstichting national guide gives 1912 and explicitly calls this the oldest shellbark hickory in the Netherlands. Both agree on species, garden and (by matched coordinates) the same physical tree; they disagree by 38 years on planting date. The 'oldest in the country' superlative only makes sense under the 1912 date, so that may be the more carefully sourced figure (the Bomenstichting register requires 80+ years for monumental status, which the tree would fail under a 1950 planting), but this pass did not resolve which is correct. Species note: shellbark hickory is genuinely rare in the Netherlands, native to the eastern US, related to pecan, produces round edible sweet nuts inside a toxic-looking husk, leaves release a strong scent when rubbed. Do not present a single confident age until the conflict is resolved or a tie-breaking source found.
curation_status_note: flagged for the age discrepancy above; species/location/existence are solid (two sources agree).

name: The Turner's Oak of the Hortus
age_estimate: roughly 131 to 161 years (sources disagree on planting year)

location.address: Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam, Plantage Middenlaan 2A, 1018 DD Amsterdam

verified_sources: https://maps.amsterdam.nl/bomen_bijzonder/ (Gemeente Amsterdam Bijzondere Bomen register, dataset 561, register_id N1778, plant year 1865, status Beschermwaardige houtopstand, owner listed as Particulier i.e. the Hortus's own private foundation rather than the municipality)

https://www.bomenstichting.nl/images/Mon_bomen_Amsterdam_2021_WEB.pdf (Bomenstichting guide, entry 'Oostenrijkse of wintergroene eik, Quercus x turneri Pseudoturneri, NR 1679235 op monumentalebomen.nl, PLANTJAAR 1895, HORTUS BOTANICUS AMSTERDAM')
access: Paid entry, Hortus Botanicus ticket required
verify_notes: SOURCE CONFLICT: register says planted 1865, Bomenstichting guide says 1895, a 30-year gap; both agree on species, cultivar and garden. Deliver flagged with the range rather than picking a winner. Genuinely distinctive species: a half-evergreen hybrid raised in England from holm oak x pedunculate oak, slow growing, tops out around 10m, keeps its leaves through most of winter and drops them only when new growth pushes them off in spring (unusual visual trait worth leading a story with), acorns hang on long stalks, and the graft union is visible about 30cm above ground. This is the same species already present at bru_011 in Brussels (Turner's Oak, Quercus x turneri) so the canonical common name is confirmed consistent with existing site usage.
curation_status_note: flagged for the age discrepancy above; species/location/existence are solid (two sources agree).

name: The Ginkgo of the Hortus
age_estimate: roughly 96 to 136 years (sources disagree, and the exact specimen match is uncertain)

location.address: Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam, Plantage Middenlaan 2A, 1018 DD Amsterdam

verified_sources: https://maps.amsterdam.nl/bomen_bijzonder/ (Gemeente Amsterdam Bijzondere Bomen register, dataset 561, register_id N1771, plant year 1930, trunk girth 321 cm, status Beschermwaardige houtopstand; a second, thinner Ginkgo N1770 also sits within 15m at 52.3665849,4.9084592, plant year 1930, girth not recorded)

https://www.bomenstichting.nl/images/Mon_bomen_Amsterdam_2021_WEB.pdf (Bomenstichting guide, entry 'Japanse notenboom, Ginkgo biloba, NR 1686147 op monumentalebomen.nl, PLANTJAAR 1890-1900, HORTUS BOTANICUS AMSTERDAM')
access: Paid entry, Hortus Botanicus ticket required
verify_notes: WEAKER MATCH THAN THE OTHER HORTUS ENTRIES, flag accordingly. The Bomenstichting guide independently confirms a mature, registered ginkgo at Hortus Botanicus planted 1890-1900, but the municipal register has TWO ginkgo entries in the immediate area (N1771 and N1770), both dated 1930, neither matching the guide's 1890s date exactly. Pinned on N1771 (the thicker of the two, 321cm girth, more consistent with an older tree despite the register's later date) as the best guess, but this pass could not conclusively prove N1771 is the specific tree the Bomenstichting guide describes rather than N1770 or a tree since removed. Species story material regardless: ginkgo is a 250-million-year-old lineage that outlived the dinosaurs, the oldest living ginkgos are around 1000 years old, trees are single-sex and female ones (which this pass could not determine) drop foul-smelling seeds after 20-50 years of maturity. Given the location and match uncertainty, a future pass should try to resolve which specific tree via Hortus's own plant database (as was done for ams_005's cycad) before this ships with full confidence.
curation_status_note: flagged for both the age discrepancy and the uncertain specimen match; do not treat the coordinate as more certain than 'this general spot in the Hortus'.
